claims.statement: The view layer follows a two-level convention: a result-rendered page under web/ or web/admin/ (the @Result location) holds only a page directive plus static <%@include%> directives, while the actual markup lives in a fragment under web/include/ — for example web/home.jsp includes include/header.jsp, top.jsp, search.jsp, home/homePage.jsp and footer.jsp, and web/login.jsp includes include/loginPage.jsp.

Storefront pages assemble fragments in a fixed order — header.jsp, top.jsp, a search header (search.jsp or simpleSearch.jsp), the page's own domain fragment, then footer.jsp; web/login.jsp is the only HTML page that omits top.jsp and the search header, and web/buy.jsp and web/alipay.jsp include top.jsp with neither search fragment.

The admin screens use a separate, disjoint include family: web/admin/*.jsp compose include/admin/adminHeader.jsp and adminNavigator.jsp with inline markup, the five paged list pages additionally include include/admin/adminPage.jsp, and no admin page includes the storefront header/top/footer fragments.

The four admin edit pages (editCategory.jsp, editProduct.jsp, editProperty.jsp, editPropertyValue.jsp) include only adminHeader.jsp and adminNavigator.jsp and never include include/admin/adminFooter.jsp, so the </body></html> that fragment owns is not emitted on those pages.

Because composition uses the translation-time <%@include%> directive, a page and its fragments form one JSP translation unit in which taglib declarations are shared: include/header.jsp declares c/fmt/fn once for all storefront pages, and fragments such as include/home/homepageCategoryProducts.jsp and include/admin/adminPage.jsp use prefixes they do not declare themselves, so a fragment cannot be compiled independently of its including page.

Every page and fragment repeats the identical page directive (contentType text/html;charset=UTF-8, language java, pageEncoding UTF-8, isELIgnored false); isELIgnored="false" is what makes every ${...} expression in the tree evaluate rather than print literally.

The html/head/body (and admin document) shell is split between fragments rather than owned by the page: include/header.jsp opens it and include/footer.jsp closes it, while include/admin/adminHeader.jsp opens the admin document and include/admin/adminFooter.jsp closes it.

The shells carry the page-wide JavaScript that fragments rely on — formatMoney/checkEmpty plus the div.productDetailDiv/div.productReviewDiv toggles in include/header.jsp, checkEmpty/checkNumber/checkInt and the deleteLink confirm handler in include/admin/adminHeader.jsp — and include/modal.jsp is pulled in only through include/footer.jsp, supplying the #loginModal and #deleteConfirmModal markup that fragments such as include/product/imgAndInfo.jsp and include/cart/cartPage.jsp open from their own scripts.

List rendering is done with c:forEach over the list properties declared on Action4Pojo and populated by each action: categories, products, orders, orderItems, properties, users, reviews, productSingleImages, productDetailImages and propertyValues.

The fragments also traverse transient per-request collections and associations nested inside the entities — category.products, Category.productsByRow, product.productSingleImages, product.productDetailImages and order.orderItems — which are populated by the service layer rather than persisted.

varStatus serves three distinct rendering jobs in the view tree: limiting rows (first N products per category, first four categories, the categorycount limit), taking fixed windows of the shared session category list in the two search fragments (positions 5-8 and 8-11), and emitting grouped-table cells such as quantity/total/action buttons only on the first item row with rowspan equal to fn:length(o.orderItems).

Three session attributes reach the fragments: user (put by ForeAction#login/#loginAjax and removed by #logout, read by include/top.jsp), cs (the full category list put by CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor, read by include/search.jsp and include/simpleSearch.jsp) and cartTotalItemNumber (computed per /fore* request by CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor, read by include/top.jsp); the session key orderItems is read by the forecreateOrder action, not by any view.

include/admin/adminPage.jsp is the only pager in the application and it binds the Page bean through EL names page.param, page.totalPage, page.total, page.start, page.count, page.last, page.hasNext and the misspelled page.hasPreviouse, whose spelling comes from the getter Page.isHasPreviouse(); its links are relative to the current action URL and re-append page.param so a page change preserves the filter.

The fragments read request parameters to carry state the action does not republish: param.keyword repopulates the search input, param.sort highlights the active sort column, param.total supplies the amount shown and echoed into the forepayed link, param.showonly switches reviewPage between the read-only review list and the review form, and param.categorycount is a limiting test parameter defaulting to 100 rows.

include/search.jsp and include/simpleSearch.jsp build the logo link from the EL expression ${contextPath}, a property declared with a getter on Action4Parameter that no code path in src/ or web/WEB-INF/web.xml assigns, so the rendered href is empty and the logo points at the current URL.

Dynamic image URLs in the markup are relative, context-path-free and id-keyed per directory — img/category/<category.id>.jpg, img/productSingle/<pi.id>.jpg, img/productSingle_small/<pi.id>.jpg, img/productSingle_middle/<firstProductImage.id>.jpg and img/productDetail/<pi.id>.jpg — with include/admin/adminNavigator.jsp the only place that prefixes an asset with ../.

Those relative asset paths only resolve because a dispatcher forward keeps the root-level action URL (every action is declared under @Namespace("/") with a flat @Action value and the context path is "/"), so markup inside web/admin/listCategory.jsp is served at /admin_category_list and img/... resolves against /; requesting /admin/listCategory.jsp directly re-bases the same relative URLs below /admin/ and breaks the images.

web/success.jsp and web/fail.jsp are not HTML views but literal AJAX response bodies (the words success and fail) returned by forecheckLogin, foreloginAjax, foreaddCart, forechangeOrderItem and foredeleteOrderItem; storefront scripts compare the response text against the literal "success", so changing that word breaks asynchronous interactions with no server-side error.

Several view entry points are reached without any action invocation and therefore without the interceptor stack: login.jsp/register.jsp/registerSuccess.jsp and the whole web/admin/** tree can be requested by name (rendering with empty EL data), the img/css/js trees are served as static resources, and AuthInterceptor inspects only URIs starting with /fore so no admin page or admin_* endpoint is protected by the pipeline.

For the root path two mechanisms exist: web/index.jsp performs a scriptlet response.sendRedirect("/forehome") while StartJetty installs an exact-match RewriteHandler rule that rewrites only the target "/" to /forehome (there is no welcome-file-list), so index.jsp is reached only when requested by name and its absolute redirect target would fall outside the application under a different context path.

The static asset tree is served by the container from web/: img/ (category, lunbo, productDetail, productSingle, productSingle_middle, productSingle_small, site), css/ (bootstrap/3.3.6 plus fonts, fore/style.css for the storefront, back/style.css for admin) and js/ (bootstrap/3.3.6 and an unreferenced jquery/3.3.1); both shells load jQuery 2.0.0 from http://libs.baidu.com, and adminHeader.jsp's Bootstrap CSS href starts with a dot ('.css/bootstrap/3.3.6/bootstrap.min.css') so it cannot resolve, leaving the admin screens styled by css/back/style.css alone.

The fragments never escape output (no <c:out>, no escapeXml, only raw ${...} with isELIgnored="false"); the application's only escaping is action-side HtmlUtils.htmlEscape on user.name in ForeAction#register/#login/#loginAjax and on review.content in ForeAction#doreview, so any user-controlled value the views print is only safe if the action behind it escaped it.

The rule a new view must follow is: declare its @Result location in Action4Result's @Results block (web/<name>.jsp for storefront, web/admin/<name>.jsp for admin), create that page as a thin assembler of the existing include chain, and put the markup in a fragment under web/include/<domain>/ named <page>Page.jsp after the page it backs — as web/include/cart/cartPage.jsp backs web/cart.jsp and web/include/home/homePage.jsp backs web/home.jsp.

include/productsBySearch.jsp gates its no-match block on ${empty ps} while the loop actually renders ${products}, and no member of that translation unit (searchResult.jsp with header, top, search, searchResultPage, productsBySearch and footer) ever sets a ps attribute, so the condition is always true.

Nothing in the repository renders a JSP in a test: the single test class only loads the Spring context and queries/deletes Category rows, so a fragment, EL or include change can only be verified by walking the manual smoke path against the running application.
